name: NY-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+24 partisan lean makes a Republican win extremely unlikely
Hakeem Jeffries is a top-ranking House Democrat with a $15 million war chest and $5 million on hand
Republican challenger Lewis Mizrahi shows no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%
model.rationale: A D+24 Brooklyn-based district, an incumbent who is one of the most prominent Democrats in the House, and a massive fundraising edge leave no credible path for the Republican challenger, who has shown no measurable financial support. Markets and fundamentals agree this is not competitive.
model.watch: The only meaningful uncertainty is turnout in a low-profile race; a dramatic national wave or Jeffries being drawn into a different district could matter, but neither is indicated by current evidence.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, seeks another term in a heavily Democratic New York City district with a D+24 partisan lean. He has raised nearly $15 million and holds $5 million on hand, an enormous advantage over Republican Lewis Mizrahi, who reports no fundraising and draws no outside spending on either side. No general-election polls or expert ratings exist for the race, which is typical for contests this lopsided.

Prediction markets put the Democratic side near 97%, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The main question is not the winner but the margin, which depends on turnout in a race receiving little attention. All available evidence points to a comfortable Democratic victory.
